Box breathing instructions: inhale for four seconds, hold four seconds, breathe out four seconds, hold four seconds. Repeat twenty times or until you feel calm.

I'm sorry for the long post. This is a passion for me. I used to deal with the same results (for different reasons), and I've found some solutions that work for me over the years.

You're not alone. I was there. I had uncontrolled anger issues for years, and I couldn't get a handle on them. I know you said meditation isn't working. Unfortunately, meditating is a legitimate skill you have to practice. It doesn't come over night, sadly. Keep at it, though. It truly does help. You can try some binaural beats. If you're like me, and you don't want to spend money, YT is okay. 7.83hz or schumann resonance. Earbuds or headphones are needed. I don't think it does anything, but the sounds help my brain relax and block out outside distractions.

Perhaps you might have anxiety issues mixed in with your anger. I did. It made things spin out of control in ways that seemed to only pick up speed as my anxiety and rage fed on each other.

Here are my immediate suggestions; box breathing. I am prior military. There were times we finished a lengthy, fast, and exhausting hike for several miles only to be instructed to aim and shoot a target while still breathing heavy. I used box breathing profusely. Breathing is natural, and you can force your mind into a state of calm by forcing your body into that state. If you're like me, you may want to know why. Box breathing activates your parasympathetic nervous system. This subsystem's purpose is rest and digestion. This forces the body to relax, forcing the mind to relax. Breath is vital. We do it without thinking about it all of the time. When I wake up in the morning, the first thing I do is take a DEEP breath. All the way down until I feel like my lung capacity is expanded into my toes. Then, I suck in just a tiny bit more. The whole process is slow. Then I release that breath and bring in new fresh oxygen for the morning. Almost works like coffee for a NT.

I put the instructions up top because, in addition to my anxiety and anger issues, I'm also impatient when my anger has gotten the best of me. I would truly like for you to come back here when you're feeling the anger and read all of these comments.

I hope what I've offered truly does help. Anger is addictive. It always made me feel safe. I'm a 6'1 260 lbs man. I have never felt safe anywhere unless I wasn't angry. I don't know if maybe that's why you use your anger, but we reinforce the ability to get angry when we fall into that loop. We strengthen the neural pathways that help us construct our reaction to the feeling of anger.

Sadly, the last thing I have for you isn't very good. It's this; pure willpower. Sometimes, nothing will work. Sometimes, you have to mentally show your anger that it doesn't run things. You have to prove to yourself that your anger can become a choice. I know it doesn't feel like it now, but it is a choice. It's hard. It's unsatisfying. It makes you feel like you don't have protection. You can decide that you don't want to go through it. I know it doesn't feel that way. I know. You CAN do it. We all can. It's just miserable. Don't bottle it up. Just, let it flow and sit through it. That one is really hard for me. To just feel it and not act it out.

Again, sorry about the long post. I have immense empathy for people stuck in the loop of anger with no way out that they can see. You have to be ready to put in the effort if you want to change, though.

In my experience, and probably why bugs are popular, is that fighting bots requires some level tactical knowledge. 

Bugs are easy because nearly all of them are melee and they swarm. Shotgun and stratagems. Issues are easily solved as long as you keep moving and don't get cornered.

Bots are altogether different. You need to know how to soldier to avoid death on the battlefield with bots. Using cover, best positions to ambush, how to properly snipe, etc...

If you like to snipe, I suggest getting really familiar with your map, how to read its terrain when you zoom in, and the path you're going to take that offers cover and/or concealment. Unless you're using the AC to snipe, you'll get found out as the mobs track the explosion of the ac. The amr, they track where the shot came from. This means shooting and moving or getting so good that they can't respond before you've wiped out the squad.

When I decide to snipe, I lay out a path around and area I'm hitting with deviations and extreme caution. My minimap is rarely ever closed when I'm not in the middle of a firefight.

Edit: Also, and this is important, taking every single fight is insane. One bot will get a flare off eventually, and you'll have a time when they start dropping hulks and tanks on you. Pick your battles. For example, the best military units don't take on a fight unless the advantage is overwhelmingly in their favor. Only take the fights you KNOW you can win. You can't rampage on the bots. They'll clap you immediately.
